w: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.

A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.

Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro. Coming from 1.x: 2.0 saves in new formats – update on Skiff's own page (it backs up and converts), or back up in its editor first.
The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.
Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.
A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.
A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.

A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.
Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.
A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.
Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.
A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.
A six-track generative synth for the M-VAVE FM-1. Play 272 Biomes, let 14 Itinera dreams travel for up to four hours, arrange with Journey, and record six mono voices plus the stereo mix over USB.

Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.

An ambient drone instrument: tap a key to latch a drone, a note or a chord in your key. Three layers a voice into a big reverb with shimmer and freeze; GLINT's icy FM bells on top, by hand, arpeggio or sequence; BASS a deep line below, held or sequenced; three LFOs keep it all moving.
Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.

Ambient as a living window: cherry petals on a river, koi in a pond, fireflies under a real moon, and every movement a note. Set it down and let it play; the keys play along, the knobs shape the scene.

A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.
A questionable musical instrument: ten artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.

Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.

A drone synth inspired by the SOMA Lyra-8, Moog Subharmonicon and Stylophone CPM DS-2. Two virtual-analog drones that breathe and drift on their own, with presets for instant ambient textures and full controls to push them into harsh, beating, self-oscillating sound.
A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.

SPAMPY 1.0: a five-track synthwave FM-1 firmware with 170 synth presets, 44 drum kits including KAVINSKY, scenes, effects, new NEON arpeggiator and Slicer modes, extended envelope controls for non-digital engines, and 5 built-in arcade games.
The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

Generative 1970s Berlin School: two sequencers drift against each other over a drone, in eight endless pieces. Play a melody on the white keys and the lead answers it, takes it as its theme and grows new ideas from it.
A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.
A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.

Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.
SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

An eight-track groovebox for sound design: thirteen synth engines, struck percussion and 33 drum machines after the Machinedrum, on an influence grid where any track can trigger, excite or modulate any other.
A groovebox inspired by the OP-XY: eight tracks on nine engines, step tricks and locks, weave, a conductor and throws.

A 12-bit sampler after the E-mu SP-1200: sample on the FM-1 itself (a computer or phone plays into it over USB) or in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), and it plays on its own. Gritty and unsmoothed, with loops and songs.
A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.
An 8-voice virtual analog tweak synth: authentic 4-pole resonant filter, dual sub-oscillator, ADSR envelopes, 64-step sequencer, and hands-on live performance controls.

A four-track groovebox: an acid bass or a Juno-style poly, physical modelling, two dozen synthesis models and a drum synth. A 64-step sequencer with song mode, generators that write parts on one chord plan, pixel characters, and USB audio with six stems, MIDI out and DAW sync.
One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.
A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.
A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.

A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.
A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.
Mellotron-style tape sounds, coloured with effects and lo-fi tape: flutes, strings and choirs as on the old tape frames, played from the keys.

Dark-music firmware for the FM-1: 21 genres, 210 pieces, dark techno to dark ambient and darkwave. Wander evolves it on its own. Arp, Dice, step editor, new visuals, simpler settings, bigger text. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).
Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.

One firmware, many synths: hold HOME and pick CS-1, Scintilla (the Elka Synthex), OberVave or a sine, no reflashing. Add PROPHET, B3 ORGAN, Niagara Drift, ARTIHIVE, FM-106, FM-1 SID, AMB-1, FoMni, MONK-1, FiMba-1, GATOR, DUB-1, FMINI-1, FM6 or ATEK303 from the page with one click, and your own…

An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.

Composing through systems on the FM-1. Thirteen generators, or your own steps, make parts that follow, answer and share one harmony. Sections, entries and a shape for the whole piece let a project unfold over minutes or hours. Play it by hand, or let it play.

A groovebox that plays itself while you steer it: nineteen genres, FM pad, bass, acid and pluck voices, drums with a step sequencer, an auto-DJ, effects you play on the keys, scenes, and a Jam page to play along. Store your pieces, and share them through the online library.

An electric piano, vibraphone and marimba, physically modelled, no samples, with drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb (hall, plate, infinite), tap tempo and MIDI clock sync, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales and presets.
Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.

Runs on the latest FM-1 chip. A bass synth for DnB, dubstep, dub and techno: deep subs, reese, growls and 808s. Two of nine engines play together, the keys change the wobble live, and one button plus a knob puts an LFO on any setting. With drums, a bass sequencer and live FX pads.

Long dark screaming ambient from the frozen Arctic. A living feedback loop creeps out of the cold and grows into a howl. Drones drift over the tundra as wind and every sound keeps moving after you let go. Four tracks, nine sound sources, endless reverb, shimmer and runaway echoes.

A ultra-refined Chiptune music editor, featuring over 35 classic chips such as NES, Gameboy, heck even the Sunsoft 5B! Pages with their own meter, tempo and glide, so waltzes and 7/8 grooves are easy. Gimmick fans rejoice!

An ambient lofi machine on 64 of its author's own pedal recordings: three synths, each with a piano roll, eight patterns, its own reverb, delay or tape echo and motion; huge shared reverbs, colour and old media over the whole mix; a chord machine and an arpeggiator, sixteen scenes, a song mode.

A slow, cinematic space drone to wander through. Its voices drift in and out on their own, and the black keys call them in. Every white key fits the scene's key, so nothing sounds wrong. A few notes looped with REC carry on when PRESET moves to a new scene: the drone glides there over 12 seconds…
SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind. Test builds: back up first.

Six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, parameter locks and slides. Forked from Hortator, with sounds ported from MONO2K.
Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.
Winamp 2.x on the FM-1, built on SLOOP: your sounds as a playlist, four tracks you record as loops, effects on sliders and a visualizer made of lines. The real firmware plays in a 3D simulator first.

A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a BBD ensemble and a phaser per sound. Now on four tracks with a mixer, delay, reverb, drive, a master and the step sequencer.

A pocket tracker for chiptune and IDM: six tracks of pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kits and samples. Chain patterns into songs, chop breaks, and play 64 live effects (with K-GLITCH's DESTROY and BEAT), a filter and an FX sequencer.
Twelve singers, from Jerry the monk to Snider the punk, each in its own voice: MonkSynth's formant voices, played with velocity and pressure from the FM-1's own keys.

An ambient worship synth. Each scene layers four lush voices in any major key around a crystal orbit home screen: pads, plucks, piano and swells. Shape them with drive, tone, granular clouds, shimmer, reverb and delay, then play live over the scene or record into it.

A six-track groovebox written from scratch: TR drums from Plaits' 808 and 909 models, a sampler with a 16-slice slicer, a bass and three free tracks (analog, 6-op FM, 303 acid), scenes and fills, all at 44.1 kHz.

Generative ambient: four editable layers from 64 sound recipes, 24 worlds, 24 motifs and 32 scales. GROW varies the phrases, seven EVOLVE processes change them over time. Felucca's sound pages stay. Built on Felucca 1.6.1.

A MULTIMORPHING bitimbral synth: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound. Ten engines including wavetables, twin filters, effects and a mod matrix. Layer, dual or stereo mode. Velocity sensitivity and aftertouch. Dual core.

The FM-1 becomes a Prophet-600: 255 sounds (the 100 factory programs, 100 from the free 2022 collection, 55 of its own), a web editor in 7 languages with a panel inspired by the Prophet-600, four tracks with sequencer, arpeggiator, morph and two insert effects each. Based on Felucca.

An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.

Explore sound with your Blop: one-finger chords from 38 grids, chord rhythms, a bass with its own riffs and a few discreet drums with sidechain, while a little creature swims to your chords in an aquarium on the screen. Chords and bass go out as MIDI over USB.

Rhythmic noise, power noise, industrial and IDM after the Elektron Digitone II: six tracks, four machines (4-OP, DRUM, WAVY, HIVE), parameter locks on a 16-step sequencer, a looper, send effects and USB audio.
A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.

Generative music for the FM-1: it composes as it plays, melody, bass, accompaniment and percussion shaped by music theory out of controlled randomness. Pick a composer or one of 86 genres across eight decades and it plays in that manner, endlessly and never twice the same.

CARNAC OS is a dual-timbral wavetable synth inspired by neolithic monuments and forgotten rituals. Built for deep sound design and immediate control, with a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer and a J6-style chord arp. The PCM waves need a separate installer: get it from my GitHub page.

A generative Irish ambient instrument: harps in a jig's threes and a flute over a drone, with surf, wind and rain. Eight pieces play themselves for ever; play along on its keys, a keyboard or a DAW. Its visualiser paints it as an Irish landscape, and its site shows how to build that into a touch…
You're making acid, baby! Smash that LFO button until you hear something you like, and then twist those knobs! Now with 100% more FX! A truly trippy experience! Built on Chipbox.

A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.

The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.
A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder. 56 factory sounds, a MIDI control for every knob, and a free browser editor that plays it over USB-MIDI.
SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.
Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.

Multi-engine synth firmware with DRONE, STASIS texture capture, Pair Morph, and per-track Random Morph and Morph Journey for evolving, ambient and experimental sound design. Sequencer, MIDI Learn, USB audio.
X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.
A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.
A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.

A pocket arranger after the QY70: pick a style, play three keys for a chord and a band of eight follows, songs from sections, General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, and a General MIDI module over MIDI in.

A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle, their real strokes on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys and 31 rhythms from the literature. Played alone: a berimbau with its caxixi, a buzzing tanpura and a breathing shruti box. Built on fm1-base.
A ten-track groovebox where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, the 303, sixteen clips a track, scatter effects and four master knobs you assign. Built on X0X.

NEW: two drum tracks. Four synths (one a Minimoog-style MUUG with 100 sounds, plus a light LITE synth) and two drum kits play at once, and the FM-1 records 8 channels into your DAW over USB: the stereo master plus each of the six tracks. A SLOOP 2.8 groovebox with the fixes of 2.8.4, 64 steps…

Draw your own waveforms, morph between sounds, and bring them to life with modulation, evolving textures, and powerful effects. From warm analog-inspired tones to wild experimental soundscapes, ETCH puts sound design right at your fingertips.

An experimental, self-playing wavetable instrument for generative, evolving soundscapes. Four PPG-style oscillators, Serge-style function generators, sample-and-holds and logic, patched through mod and gate matrices. 12 bit, 22kHz, green phosphor CRT, Fairlight-style pages.

The 1981 Elka Synthex on the FM-1: all 80 factory sounds, Paul Wiffen's laser harp among them, checked sample by sample against the original. Two layers of 8 voices (single, split, double), poly, mono or unison, chorus and reverb, and the four knobs edit what is on the screen.

Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs measured on real chips, a GoatTracker 2 tracker and step sequencer with slide and accent, .sid playback with live tweaks, LAB for sounds with step tables and LFOs, patches from an AI chat or SidStation banks, Bluetooth MIDI, and Live Link in a browser.
Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP: original drums and icons and four factory songs. A test release: not yet fully tested on the device.
A chord and string instrument: 16 synthesized sounds, 50 chord styles, editable voicings, guitar tunings, and Freeplay, Strum and Arp modes with partial-chord pulses.
A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.

A beat dojo for scratch DJs and beatmakers: boom bap, lo-fi and breaks from 16 rhythm families with swing and fills, an eight-lane 32-step sequencer, punch-in effects you record bar by bar, a bass voice. Sound banks and editor in the browser.

Eight-voice experimental drone and polyphonic FM synthesizer with four interacting pairs, envelopes, legato glide, hyper LFO, stereo motion, dual modulated delay and a 1-16 step arpeggiator and sequencer. Artistically inspired by SOMA LYRA-8; independently developed.

An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.

A super powerful drum synth and sequencer that started as a port of the Erica Synths LXR-02 and kept going. Make a beat in two minutes, then dig into 29 sound engines, deep effects, generative sequencing, live performance tricks, MIDI control and 8-channel USB audio.
Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins. A beta.

A sad wavetable synth played by a pixel blob in a rainy room: its eyes are the filter, its mouth the envelope, its tears the delay. Gloomy beats with auto-bass, an arpeggiator, a pattern sequencer, twelve punch effects on the black keys, and presets of your own.
The Sega Genesis / Mega Drive's Yamaha YM2612: six channels of 4-operator FM. Its web app takes patches from game music (VGM) and OPM files and streams VGM tunes to the FM-1 to play.

An LLM-written expansion of Felucca with multiple patterns per track, per-step patch switching, multiple synth engines that emulate the Nord Lead and parts of the SH-4d and Elektron Digitone II, and no samples.

A chord groovebox after the Roland J-6: 100 chord sets, 9 phrase styles with 12 variations each and a 64-pattern step sequencer, on a four-voice Juno-style synth from Clipper with chorus, delay and reverb. A chord map on the screen shows which chord sits on which key. Built on Dinghy.
The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.

Hortator's eight-track groovebox taken further: ORB Remix with 256 pattern mappings, the TB-3PO acid melody generator with 22 scales, more acid waveshaping, four bipolar LFOs and Grids rhythms copied into editable steps.
A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.

A six-track instrument for sound exploration and live layering. Eight engines span FM, acid bass, textures and hybrid drums. Shape sounds with granular processing, filters and effects; record free loops, build sequences, add automatic accompaniment and morph between snapshots. Based on Tonitor.

Microtonic, for the FM-1! Roll the dice for a kit, build one from scratch, or bring in your Microtonic presets and patterns. Share kits and patterns as files, and send it all to your Teenage Engineering PO-32! Built on Chipbox!
A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.
An original four-part groovebox with a 1990s workflow: three melodic parts and a 16-lane drum part, 128 melodic presets, eight drum kits, song arrangement, an arpeggiator and recorded knob moves.

Generative 90s eurodance, pickled in 1995. Press PLAY and Sill writes a song and plays it: offbeat basses, piano and supersaw stabs, a chorus hook with a choir and a key change for the last chorus. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, break it down, push the key up and play the hook yourself.

A granular sampler: a few seconds of any sound become slow clouds, sparkles, tape loops and swells, played from the keys and knobs. 14 factory sounds, your own samples (or recorded over USB), filter, delay, reverb and tape, and a companion web app for samples, presets and recording.
A MIDI controller: notes in any scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own when nothing is connected.

A ProTracker-style pocket studio: DX7 FM, JUNO-106, TB-303, chip, sampler and FUSION instruments side by side, 16 voices on both cores, a loop station, a two-deck DJ mode, punch-in effects and over 500 built-in instruments.

Four synth and sampler tracks and a drum track on 14 engines, among them wavetable, 6-op FM, tape scrub, granular and a slicer; a 64-step sequencer, a chord progression generator, macros and sidechain ducking.

The SLOOP groovebox for the M-VAVE FM-1, forked for dub: a four-band isolator with mute bands, a bipolar DJ filter, per-track echo throws, a tape echo with free time or synced divisions, an independent siren voice, skank, accents and slides — with a sound-system bank of 180 genre presets (ska to…

Grooves in chrome: filtered, pumping, robotic. Press PLAY and Daurade plays a filtered loop that opens over sixteen bars, a mix that pumps on every kick, a robot voice singing the hook and crisp drums. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, drop it, set off a solo or play the lead yourself.

An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.

A karaoke robot with a band: it sings songs from karaoke and MIDI files, or lines you type, to the notes you play. Its face is the voice. Keys, bass and drums play along, with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects.

A riffbox for rock and metal: real guitar, bass and drum samples, an amp engine with cabinet IRs, pedals and guitar effects, plus all of SLOOP's synth engines. Bend strings, play whammy, wah and palm mutes live, record on the 4-track and turn riffs into songs.

A 12-voice wavetable synth: two oscillators a voice, a resonant filter, two envelopes, an LFO, four effects, an arpeggiator and two step sequencers for chords and counterpoint; load your own Serum, WaveEdit, Ableton or Surge tables.
Jam Playground plays a new song the moment you turn the FM-1 on. Four synths and eleven drums sound together. Turn a knob to change the vibe, the scale, a sound, or an effect, and play along.

A minimal Elektron-style groovebox: four tracks, patterns in banks A to E, parameter locks, trig conditions, chains, an arpeggiator per track and per-pattern kits on the MONOFM sound core. A hard fork of Felucca.

An Amen break chopper for the FM-1: eight classic breaks cut into 16 slices on the white keys, hold a key to loop it. Black keys are momentary pads for rolls, reverse, freeze, tape stop, gate, filter and dub throws. A generator rearranges the break live, with a four-slot FX chain and a DJ filter.

A three-channel groovebox: a Polivoks-style duophonic synth (PLVKS), an Elka-style sample drum machine with a step sequencer, and a dub siren, with BBD echoes, per-channel character effects, arp, scales and a mixer with panning.

A groovebox for lively mediæval dance music: hurdy-gurdy, lutes, shawms and frame drums over drones, four tracks with 64-step sequencers, mediæval modes and temperaments, and velocity from the FM-1's own keys. Built on GHOULBOX and Felucca.

SPELLBOX turns the FM-1 into a talking spelling toy after the 1978 Speak & Spell: an 8-character fluorescent display, a 10-pole LPC voice at 8 kHz through an 8-bit DAC, and the SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE and MYSTERY WORD games over four levels, with the keys as an A-to-Z keyboard. SPEAK…

Play the VIBE FM VST plugin with your FM-1. Install this and the FM-1 is the controller: the keys play, KNOB 1-4 and every button do in the plugin what they do on the FM-1 – SLOOP, Felucca, OberVave and the other converted firmwares feel like home, in your DAW, in the Web Player and on the VIBE FM. The sound comes from the plugin, not the FM-1. Plain MIDI: any synth or DAW can learn it too.

A groovebox around one engine, ChoralRoot's FM TONE: eight tracks, p-locks and preset sound locks, conditions, ratchets, chords, and MIDI FX for generative patterns and for reworking the ones you have. Bluetooth MIDI, and recording over USB audio.
Four Track Groovebox with a dungeon crawler cooked into the home screen for the visualizer. Create your party from 8 heroes, store up to 6 sequences then string them together in Song mode!
A bard's instrument for LARP, medieval and high fantasy: recorder, hurdy-gurdy, harp and a tavern kit on four tracks, encounters and songs for the table. "Mother Melody hears thy song."

A MOD / XM tracker, sampler and groovebox: play, write and save FastTracker 2 and ProTracker songs on the FM-1, up to 32 channels, with a ProTracker mode for MODs and a song manager in the browser for moving songs to and from the computer.

BEETLE transforms the FM-1 into a powerful 6-channel music workstation. Create beats, design sounds with retro-inspired synth engines, sequence entire songs, and perform with live effects. A complete pocket-sized tracker, drum machine, and synthesizer. Built for creativity, born out of passion.

Noise and modeling synth with GM-style presets (4 banks, 512) and a 4-track tape recorder: each voice a live Chua circuit or noise program, through vactrol gates into resonators and piano, drum, voice, flute, brass, bowed, reed and bird waveguides, with temple, cathedral and mosque reverbs. GM…

A live jungle tool built around classic breaks (Amen, Apache, Think) and your own. Hold white keys for rolls, builds, echo and Akai-style metallic stretch, play hits on the black keys, and shape the break with variation, warp, ringing feedback, lo-fi, EQ, saturation and compression.
B1 turns the M-VAVE FM1 into a compact drawbar rock organ with 91 shared tonewheels, nine drawbars per registration, percussion, Leslie, B3/ROCK tones, MIDI and expressive live controls.

An eight-part multitimbral DX7 module. Every part has its own MIDI channel and up to eight layered DX7 voices, with key splits, velocity windows and 64 scenes. A master filter, shared reverb and delay, DX7 ROM import and a web configurator. Played and controlled over MIDI.

Latin and Caribbean groovebox: synthesized congas, bongos, timbales, guiro and cowbell, 14 grooves from salsa and bomba to dembow, tumbao and montuno lines over the chord you hold, generative parts in the clave, and effect scenes from a backyard to a dub.

A gamelan-inspired ensemble. Lead the core melody on the white keys and the ensemble answers: interlocking kotekan, reyong, kendang and gongs in measured Balinese and Javanese tunings, every note shimmering with ombak. Play the traditional forms, or slow it right down for meditation.

A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music. Six lanes (lead, arp, pad, bass, drums and sfx) play parts composed live in eighteen styles. You don't program steps, you mix styles: blend the next one in lane by lane, shape each lane with tracker effects and call the drop.

A monophonic macro-oscillator on the open Plaits DSP: all 24 models with harmonics, timbre and morph, an 8-slot mod matrix fed by an envelope, two LFOs, velocity, aftertouch and random, a low-pass gate, and a DRONE mode.

A generative Berlin School MIDI sequencer: a small ensemble of voices that repeat, phase against each other on loops of unequal length and earn their mutations over time. The FM-1 makes no sound with it: each voice goes out over USB on its own MIDI channel to your synths, as Berlinan for macOS…

A six-track groovebox for the FM-1, forked from Skiff: a SYNTH with analog, 303 and Plaits-style oscillators, an acid filter and OberVave presets, a Minimoog voice, classic drum models, more trig conditions, a step arpeggiator, 8-channel USB audio, a web editor and screen mirroring.

A Eurorack-style modular synth: 56 modules (VCOs, a Moog-style ladder, a Moog 960-style sequencer that plays your voices, a low pass gate, Turing, Marbles, chaos, effects) patched with cables on the FM-1 itself, a 64-step sequencer with live recording, 33 factory patches, visuals, USB audio and…

Resampling sound design. Build one sound from FM, analog or 808-style drums, play it as notes, steps or strummed chords, add 6 LFOs, 3 envelopes and 8 FX, then resample it into a new source. Every resample keeps its recipe, so a 64-sound bank of generation trees rebuilds bit for bit.

A monophonic bass synth on Cycle Exchange Synthesis: two sub-oscillators, a ladder filter, Channel EQ, eight effects from MOSFET drive to octave fuzz, a step sequencer up to 128 steps and an arpeggiator.

Firmware for dark industrial and EBM, built on Felucca. Adds the GLCH distortion engine from Glitchbox, 171 sounds and 13 drum kits, DICE to generate parts in eight styles, random sound variations, tape and digital degradation of the mix, and a manual in English and Russian.

Wanderer 1.4: author-tested synth for low-vision musicians. Protect an Anchor, evolve two layers, play 100 sounds, eight Scatter modes and a 13-pattern arp. Adaptive/steady Zoom, clear knob controls, adjustable display hold and optional audio cues.

Plays C64 SID music from HVSC on an emulated 6581 or 8580 and lets you remix every voice live: transpose, mute, solo, swap waveforms, bend envelopes and filter, add LFOs, ride the tempo. Out of the jack, as USB audio or over ASID to a real SID. MIDI clock from the tune, or the tune synced to yours.

A B3 tonewheel organ: 91 wheels, nine drawbars, key click, vibrato and chorus, percussion, overdrive, reverb and a Leslie, computed from setBfree's own data and measured against it. All 110 setBfree programs and its default MIDI controllers.
One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Etude in C major, Op. 10 No. 1, on a sampled Steinway D. Flyfish plays it and lets you shape it, practise it and move it.
A firmware for your firmwares when using the app or a high quality 24bit DX7 rompler with 16 user carts and MIDI Controller when using the FM-1 by itself. BLE and USB supported!
An unofficial parody virtual pet with a playable pentatonic keyboard. Feed, praise, clean up after and rest the pet. When he's happy, he joins your playing on bongos.

An LXR-style drum machine: eight sounds, each a synth and a sample layer, with drive, delay, reverb, filter, compressor and limiter. 16 patterns of up to 64 steps, per-track speed, locks, conditional trigs, chains and song mode, MIDI clock and CC learn. Its samples are the Sonic Potions LXR's, non-commercial licence.

A four-track groovebox that plays like a four-piece band: lead, pads, bass and drums. 40 sounds and 10 drum kits, 5 effect pedals, an arpeggiator, step and live recording, and a song sequencer where each instrument follows its own arrangement.
Pick a chord progression, press Play, and play along with drums, bass and chords. Adjust the progression, sounds and groove to build backing tracks for practicing, jamming and writing songs.

A generative drum machine on the LXR sound engine. Seven voices, kits grown from a seed in 16 characters, a 64-step sequencer with conditions and per-step pitch, patterns generated and mutated in 11 styles, MIDI notes and clock in, and nine named projects.

A band in your FM-1. Pick a spot on a map of 16 genre towns and it writes a four-piece sketch: drums, bass, keys and lead in one key. Re-roll parts, audition players, jam, morph, play punch-in effects, edit steps, save four slots. With a rhythm game played over your own drum part.
A pattern sequencer after Reason's Matrix: up to four channels of MIDI sequence data out, and a few voices built in to build the patterns with.

Live club mixing for the FM-1: four layers (lead, chord, bass, drums) that play by themselves in 20 styles while you ride them live. Blend one style into the next, build with intros and break-build-drop arcs, edit steps or play a layer by hand. All synthesised but the piano.
A side-scrolling action game with synthesized music, sound effects and character voices. Defend the dam, ride through robot city, fly to the data center and stop Mother.

Generative ambient and drone: Immaculate Permutation rolls an arrangement in one key, a pad, a sequence and a chord arpeggio under a fourth voice for your hands. Keep a sermon you like, evolve it, or reveal another.

A Mega Drive / Genesis music tracker. It emulates the YM2612 and SN76489 chips: six FM channels, three square waves and noise, with Deflemask-style effects, 128 FM presets, a drum kit on the DAC, 256 song slots, a demo song and VGM export.

A JP-8000/8080-style virtual analog on eight voices: the JT-8000 engine ported to the FM-1, with Super Saw, the JP filter, multi-effects, delay, a plate reverb, an arpeggiator and 64 programs, every knob on the JP-8080's own MIDI CCs.

A six-voice analog-style synth: AMY's emulations of the 128 Juno-60 factory patches, shaped with the AMYboard editor's patch knobs (oscillators, LFO, filter, envelopes, EQ, chorus, reverb, distortion) on eleven colour-coded pages. Plays over USB MIDI, and the AMYboard editor can edit it live.
A monosynth: one voice with analogue-modelled oscillators and five filters (ladder, diode ladder, OTA, Sallen-Key, state-variable), unison, chorus, delay and reverb, and 14 presets.

C64 music on the FM-1: a 6510 runs each tune's own code and reSID plays it, PSID and RSID. A GoatTracker 2 editor on the FM-1 itself with ten GT2 example songs, a SID synth with a sequencer and effects, and any .sid sent from the browser plays at once.

Dfam style 16-step sequencer and a drum synth: two oscillators with 16 wave types, a kick with its own sequencer, parameter locks, a sound saved per pattern, an effects chain, random pages, scales, presets and projects.
A MIDI monitor for USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth (as device and host at once): hex or words, filters, stats. Its THRU routes, each filtered, make the FM-1 a Bluetooth MIDI dongle.

A dub station for the M-VAVE FM-1: the USB/BT audio router with sloop-DUB's dub modules on top — a dub siren, a tape echo, a bipolar DJ filter and a four-band isolator, each page's four settings on K1-K4, the black keys as the live performance: the eighth turns the dub on and off, the ninth and…

An LLM-written expansion of Felucca with multiple patterns per track, per-step patch switching, multiple synth engines that emulate the Nord Lead and parts of the SH-4d and Elektron Digitone II, and no samples.

Golana's synth with a sequencer for whole songs: 64 steps a pattern, 32 programs (up to 2,048 steps), a SONGMODE that plays from a first to a last program once or on repeat, and USB MIDI out to sequence other synths.

An experimental mono-track FM cell synthesizer with programmable oscillator routing, modulation, sequencing, a vintage circuit-derived filter, VCA, wavefolding, digital fidelity reduction and reverb. A load engine models physical voltage sag and progressively shrinks resource usage under stress.
A spoon-feeding balance game with a beatless ambient soundtrack and voiced reactions. Balance a bean, guide the spoon and try to feed Travis. Every fifth bite sets off a transformation.

SPLITMILK is a performance-focused firmware that separates the keyboard into two independent instruments, with chords, arpeggiators, effects and an adjustable split. Play both instruments live over built-in drum and pad sequencers to create music without endless menu-diving.

A seven-voice drum synth on the LXR firmware's engine. Its step sequencer has per-lane length and direction. Steps have parameter locks, chance and pass conditions, so one pattern can change from pass to pass. It loads LXR-02 .SND kits, sends 10 channels of USB audio and syncs to MIDI clock.

Generative dark ambient: drones, demonic and angelic choirs, bells and 135 sound effects that keep changing by themselves across 15 worlds, with 40 melting pictures. Play bells or latch choir voices on the keys, or play and hold effects. Works on older and newer FM-1s (both flash chips).

A modular synth for the FM-1: 30 factory patches built from nested modules, from classic polysynths to drum machines, each played with four knobs per page, plus a step sequencer with patterns and songs. Build your own patches in the browser editor and send them to the FM-1 over USB.

A four-track MIDI arranger and controller for the M-VAVE FM-1. Create patterns, songs and albums, switch patterns live, route USB and Bluetooth MIDI, and play sounds with the onboard General MIDI synth.

Generative just-intonation firmware for the FM-1. Two layers of moving points wander a map of 41 scales and play the notes they pass; a rhythm without a grid drives four drums that follow the synth. Four knobs steer it, the keys play into it, and it can stream to Bluetooth speakers.

BEETLE BLUE turns your M-VAVE FM1 into a six-lane drum tracker. Build beats with BEETLE and MONOLITH kits, design custom drums, arrange songs, and perform setlists with Live Mode and hands-on effects.

A groovebox OS for M-VAVE FM-1, built on SLOOP and Felucca: seven synth parts plus drums, 24 patterns, 128 SONG positions, clearer 64-step views, live granular INSERT, selective kick ducking and MIDI THRU for external instruments. Includes a browser editor with audio preview.

Pick a style and generate a band in one press. Chords, bass, drums and melody stay in sync and play off each other. In GLO Live, use the keys to solo parts, cue fills and drops, and play effects over the groove.

Turns the FM-1 into an effects box. Sound from a computer, sent over USB, comes out of its socket through AISLING's live effects: reverb, shimmer, echo, phaser, drive, crush and more, held by key or CC. Knobs set the filter, sends and dry, and the wet sound goes back up the cable.

A backing band to play over: drums, bass, chords and a synth line follow your chords in any key and time signature, in time with a loop pedal. 160 factory jams in 16 genres, a new jam at a press, your own synth line on a piano roll, and a companion web app to edit and share jams.

Erik. Evolved. Ten Satie pieces become an evolving electronic soundtrack in five moods. Choose a tune, set the pace and blend Solo, Duet or Trio. Shape each instrument, add vinyl colour and synced delay, or simply let it play. GLO opens the quick guide.

A performance firmware built on Optimist: two synth layers on one keyboard (layer, split, blend or single), drums with a simple step sequencer, send effects, Bluetooth MIDI keyboards, and one easy to read screen with knobs 1-4 to edit all parameters. 5 engines, 32 drum kits, 135 presets.

Generative Latin grooves for the FM-1: a band on the clave in twelve styles, from salsa and mambo to bolero, bossa and tango, with sampled percussion, upright piano, brass, sax, violins and double bass. Lead the band with hits and a mambo, take the trumpet solo on the keys, or play and edit each…

Game Boy music programs on the FM-1: LSDj, the tracker, and DMGo!, the drum machine, in a Game Boy emulator on its screen, keys and knobs. Bring your own ROM: the install page puts it in, in your browser.
Two independent drum layers and Dillo, an Open303-derived acid bass, through tape echo and spring reverb: a synthesised 808 and seven sampled machines, 67 songs, 21 eras and 205 ACID phrases.

Little Sound Dj, the Game Boy tracker, on the FM-1: played from its keys and knobs, with per-channel filters, drive, lo-fi and an LFO, a shared echo, reverb and compressor, MIDI sync and colour themes. Bring your own LSDj: the project's web page adds it to this firmware on your computer.

A TB-303 style acid synth with its own pattern generator: press PLAY and a line plays. Generate, mutate and undo patterns up to 64 steps, edit steps in a piano roll, add drive, chorus, synced delay and plate reverb. The ATEK303 engine from VCV Rack with 14 oscillators and its fine tuning, 12…
USB audio interface and Bluetooth audio receiver with FX
A modular synth for the FM-1. With over 80 modules, including synth engines, samplers, filters, effects, sequencers, and generative tools, you can build, patch, and perform directly on the hardware.

A hands-on groovebox firmware for the FM-1. Shape sounds, build patterns, and find your own groove. Up to six assignable tracks, sound design, sequencing and performance. Free and open source, built on JIANT and reworked by Jazzy Rhythmer.

A singing songwriter: a pixel singer sings your songs in Japanese, consonants and all, over FM chords, bass and drums. Shape her voice with effects, harmony and five characters, write patterns or let her generate a whole song, and watch her dance. 8 song slots.

The ATEK303 acid groovebox plus a drum track on the same clock: eight synthesized TR-808/909/707 voices, no samples, a seeded 64-step generator with mutations and LOCK for both tracks, an 8x16 drum matrix, swing, three kits, drive, chorus, delay, reverb and eight factory presets.

Kris Jangle is a Christmas game for the FM-1: it plays the start of a carol and you replay it on the keys, building three notes per level up to the whole song. Four carols, three play modes from guided EASY to sound-only HARD, and Grump Mode on three misses.

Mighty Arp, from the creator of Mighty Synth Sampler, is a 4-op FM/subtractive synth built around a chance arpeggiator. Just hold a chord and let chance play the melody. 50 sounds plus a RANDOM mode that invents new ones, a 32-step sequencer, chords, effects and more.

A drone synth with velocity-sensitive keys. Press a key and a voice plays until you stop it: eight voices, thirteen sounds. Motion modes move them in your scale: single notes, chords, chord progressions, arpeggios. Chorus, delay and reverb with freeze. A mixer for drone, lead and effects.

A generative ambient firmware. FM voices through a tape echo and a plate play by themselves in seven worlds that exist nowhere. You steer from outside: a key offers something to a hidden state, the knobs change the weather, and the music answers slowly.

A hardcore kick synthesizer powerhouse and a breakbeat chopper (gabber, terror, speedcore): a heavy kick with its own synth, DISTO and SCREAM distortion, effects and twenty memories, breaks sliced on the white keys, effects on the black keys, snare, hat, clap, songs with builds and drops, a…

A sound companion for Shavasana and meditation. Guided programs on 174, 396, 432 and 528 Hz drift from theta to delta, isochronic for speakers or binaural for headphones, with breath, singing bowls and an ambient garden, then wake you gently. Play handpan, kalimba or chimes on the keys.

A control surface for coding agents, not an instrument: the keys and screen show which of your Claude Code, Codex or other command-line agents are working, finished or waiting on you, and the buttons approve, deny, interrupt and prompt them. It needs its daemon on the computer.

Turns the FM-1 into the 1947 Clavioline, an early electronic analog synthesizer. Faithfully rebuilt from the original circuit diagrams with distinctive tone-shaping stops, vibrato, knee-lever expression and vintage electronic sounds.

Expressive rhythm section ideas fast. Pick one of 19 styles and it draws patterns from that genre's feel, which keep evolving as you play, over a bass line in your key. Breaks, builds and fills on a button, a DJ filter, MIDI clock sync and USB audio stems for your DAW.

A stereo-field morphing synth. Two oscillators with eight models, a sub, noise and ring mod, two filters and two dirt stages, each with its own pan. Move the pans and the sound travels around you. A morph glides between two versions of every patch. Effects and a mod matrix. Best with headphones.

Adrift transforms the M-VAVE FM-1 into a 16-voice, 6-part Bucket-Brigade Resonator synthesizer, capable of plucked guitars, bowed cellos, buzzing sitars, granular clouds, hands-free drones, and massive unison leads.

A drum machine for the FM-1: ten synthesized drum channels, 32 patterns of up to 64 steps with p-locks, conditions, micro timing and ratchets, free recording with QUANT, beat repeat, 8 LFOs per pattern, reverb, tape delay and a master compressor. No samples, no computer needed.
